chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Frank Sebastian and how the Cotton Club got its name
summary: Sebastian came to the music store looking for musicians, saw Duke Ellington's Cotton Club advertisement and named his Culver City club after it.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Thomas Valentine, banjo?
Yeah. Where'd you get all that old stuff?
Well, these are all names that are mentioned in the McCarthy--the Big Band book.
Oh, are they? I haven't read that. The ones that I had part of...half of it was gone, and I just...
But these are...doesn't say too much about them but I just thought maybe if I mentioned the names, they might remind you of something.
Yeah, I know him, the banjo player, yeah.
Did you ever know Frank Sebastian?

Frank Sebastian? Sure, I did. He come down to... when Frank Sebastian started to open a nightclub, they come down to the music store, and they wanted to know if I had a band or anything, you know, and whether I could get...and he looked up on the wall, and there was Duke Ellington's big advertisement sheet, you know, like I had my band in there? The Cotton Club. So, he said, "That's the name we going to name it: Cotton Club."
Oh, really?
Yeah, so it was Sebastian's Cotton Club.
That's how it happened! That's interesting.
That's how he got the name. Came in. He brought down...you see, he brought down some old guy that had been a waiter for a

long...I think it was his uncle, but he seemed to have the money. Sebastian was a young guy then--and good looking! Very good looking then! And they came down there. They wanted me to...they was looking for musicians in the band. And that time I didn't have no band. I just had several, you know, but I'd send this and that and that the other, and I don't know who went out there first to play. I don't know who was the first band. Anyway, when they come down there, I had a folder from New York. It said...uh...uh: "Duke Ellington's Cottonwood...uh...uh..."
"...Cotton Club Orchestra."
"...Cotton Club Orchestra," you know. Then I had another one of that other big band was back there at that time...
Cab Calloway? Fletcher Henderson?
No. No, another one that was very popular.
Mills Blue Rhythm Band? Jimmie Lunceford? That was later, though.
[McKinney's Cotton Pickers]

No. There was another one that had a big band there. I can't think of it. They were very popular, too. Just like Duke. Anyway, it had on there, "Duke...at the Cotton Club." New York Cotton Club. And they said, "That's the name we want! Cotton Club!"
Oh, that's interesting.
